- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.33), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is trending up.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days); cap forecast increase after spike to 3–5% max.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 68–70), model often holds too high; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 2–3 periods.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward; add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast.
- For 30-day horizon, model often lags true price by 1–3 days; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment turns negative after a spike, model fails to correct; reduce forecast by 2–4% immediately after sentiment drop.
- Model tends to underestimate in early horizon (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; add 0.5–1.5% to initial forecast.
